# Level Up Makers

> A parent-run path for ages 9–14. Students make a first game, then move into real code and the Godot engine. A grown-up runs any AI help.

Level Up Makers publishes one manual now: Level Up: Make Your First Game with AI. It is a three-module path. Level Up 1 uses Microsoft MakeCode Arcade. Level 1 is free to read and print. The paperback is $34.99 at https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HQDMJ24G. The complete PDF is $15 and available now for immediate download at https://payhip.com/b/6KDfn. The Parent + Student bundle is $29 and available now for immediate download at https://payhip.com/b/NsL1H. It includes the unchanged 178-page manual plus separate printables: a 10-page workbook, badge sheets and a certificate, a Hero Card, a Game Idea Sheet, a Playtest Scorecard, a Pixel Grid, a World Map, a Level Plan Grid, a sharing checklist, and a printing and support README. Level Up 2, Real Code Quest, is coming soon and is not for sale yet. The planned price is a $19 PDF and a $34.99 paperback. Students about 10–14 read their own MakeCode Arcade game as JavaScript and Python in Levels 1–2, which work in Chrome, including on a Chromebook, then rebuild their hero in Godot 4 with GDScript in Levels 3–10, which need a Windows, Mac, or Linux computer. Each of the 10 levels ends in something playable. The free Star Catcher practice file is at https://levelupmakers.com/star-catcher/, so students who do not have the first book can join in. Level Up 3, Bring Your World to Life, is coming soon, with no price listed yet. Level Up Makers: Pocket Games is a separate coming-soon manual. Kids make retro handheld-style games in GB Studio, which is free for Windows, Mac, and Linux. It has ten levels, optional AI coding help that a parent decides, and an optional way to play a finished game on a real retro handheld cartridge-style device. Its price is coming soon. It is not for sale yet.

Students invent original characters, then move from blocks to typed code and the Godot engine. Any AI help is typed by a grown-up on the grown-up's own account. These pages do not collect children's personal information. Public pages, the free Level 1 PDF button, and the coming-soon notify links send a coarse count (event name, source label, and time) to a Cloudflare Worker. The browser turns the referring site into a short label such as facebook, direct, site, or other. The full referring address is not sent. The count uses no cookies and no third-party tracker, and it does not include an IP address, browser type, name, email, or anything about a child. It is stored in Cloudflare Analytics Engine when that Worker is deployed. levelupmakers.com itself is answered by GitHub Pages. The on-site free Level 1 PDF stays at https://levelupmakers.com/level-1/level-1-spark.pdf.

- [Home](https://levelupmakers.com/): The learning path, the free downloads, the Level Up 1 outline, what students make, the safety rules, prices for the first manual, and a Who we are section. Level Up Makers is a grandmother and grandson team. Written for parents. Free downloads on the home page: the Level 1 sample PDF, the free Level 1 PDFs for Real Code Quest and Pocket Games (both books are coming soon), the Star Catcher practice file, and the Real Code Quest practice files (hero.png and Godot starter and finished projects for Levels 5-10).
- [Review copy](https://levelupmakers.com/review/): Email gate for adult influencers and reviewers. It is for the full digital book, not a Payhip link. The automatic PDF email is not connected yet. Families should use Amazon or Payhip.
- [Books](https://levelupmakers.com/book/): Level Up: Make Your First Game with AI is available now. Paperback on Amazon ($34.99) and the complete PDF on Payhip ($15, immediate download). The same page lists Level Up 2: Real Code Quest and Level Up Makers: Pocket Games as coming soon.
- [Level Up 2: Real Code Quest](https://levelupmakers.com/real-code-quest/): Coming soon. Not for sale yet. Sequel to the first Level Up book, for students about 10–14. Levels 1–2 read a MakeCode Arcade game as JavaScript and Python in Chrome, including on a Chromebook. Levels 3–10 rebuild the hero in Godot 4 with GDScript and need a Windows, Mac, or Linux computer. Ten levels, each ending in something playable. Planned PDF $19. Planned paperback $34.99. Level 1 of this book is a free PDF at https://levelupmakers.com/real-code-quest/real-code-quest-level-1.pdf. It is the first lesson only. The free Star Catcher practice file is at https://levelupmakers.com/star-catcher/ for students who do not have the first book. Practice files for the book are listed on that page (hero.png and Godot starter and finished project zips for Levels 5-10) at https://levelupmakers.com/downloads/real-code-quest/. To be notified, email hello@levelupmakers.com. There is no form.
- [Pocket Games](https://levelupmakers.com/pocket-games/): Coming soon. Not for sale yet. Kids make retro handheld-style games in free GB Studio on Windows, Mac, or Linux, across ten levels. AI coding help is optional and a parent decides. An optional payoff is playing a finished game on a real retro handheld cartridge-style device. Price coming soon. Level 1 is a free PDF at https://levelupmakers.com/pocket-games/pocket-games-level-1.pdf. It is the first lesson only. To be notified, email hello@levelupmakers.com. There is no form.
- [Using ESA or charter school funds?](https://levelupmakers.com/funding/): How a family can ask a charter school or a state education savings account program about ordering the curriculum. The program decides. Level Up Makers cannot guarantee eligibility. The paperback is sold and shipped by Amazon. The PDF is $15 and the Parent + Student bundle is $29 on Payhip. For an invoice or a W-9, email hello@levelupmakers.com.
- [Printables](https://levelupmakers.com/printables/): Live page listing the 10-page workbook, badge sheets and certificate, Hero Card, Game Idea Sheet, Playtest Scorecard, Pixel Grid, World Map, Level Plan Grid, sharing checklist, and printing and support notes. Those files come in the $29 bundle download at https://payhip.com/b/NsL1H. They are not separate files on the page.
- [Level 1: Spark](https://levelupmakers.com/level-1/): Free chapter. Idea Forge, an original hero, and a tiny collect-it game in MakeCode Arcade, plus prompts a grown-up can paste into their own AI chat. The printable file is the free chapter only: https://levelupmakers.com/level-1/level-1-spark.pdf. The same free chapter can also be sent by email from Payhip at https://payhip.com/b/tlxyB. Payhip asks for an email. The page on this site does not. It is not the 178-page Payhip manual.
- [Star Catcher practice file](https://levelupmakers.com/star-catcher/): Free MakeCode Arcade cartridge from Level 1, for students who need a practice game before Level Up 2: Real Code Quest. Level Up 2 is coming soon and is not for sale yet. The file is https://levelupmakers.com/downloads/star-catcher-practice.png. Import it at arcade.makecode.com with Import, then Import File, or by dragging the PNG onto the editor.
- [Blog](https://levelupmakers.com/blog/): Parent guides. Includes [Coding Games for Kids 9–12: The First 5 Games a Kid Can Build](https://levelupmakers.com/blog/coding-games-for-kids-9-12/) for five beginner MakeCode Arcade games, [A Simple Homeschool Coding Plan for Ages 9–12](https://levelupmakers.com/blog/homeschool-coding-curriculum-makecode-arcade/) for a 10-week MakeCode Arcade plan, and [MakeCode Arcade vs Scratch](https://levelupmakers.com/blog/makecode-arcade-vs-scratch/) for choosing a first game tool at ages 9–13.

## Policies

- [Terms of service](https://levelupmakers.com/terms/): Rules for using the site. Level 1 is free. The paperback is sold on Amazon. The complete PDF is $15 and available now through Payhip.
- [Privacy policy](https://levelupmakers.com/privacy/): The public pages have no forms. A coarse visit count uses no cookies and no third-party tracker. We don't collect children's personal information. Amazon and Payhip run checkout.
- [Refund policy](https://levelupmakers.com/refunds/): How to ask about a Level Up Makers PDF order. Amazon handles paperback returns. Earlier orders still have a way to ask through the contact page.
- [Contact](https://levelupmakers.com/contact/): hello@levelupmakers.com. No form. Copy the address or use Email us.
